summary: Interleaved assistant fragments and stray metadata after client refresh behind corporate proxy
description: Issue summary: After a customer-side page refresh or corporate proxy failover, subsequent SSE sessions reconnect but the delivered stream contains interleaved assistant text fragments and stray metadata markers (e.g., duplicated "[meta]" tokens) that appear in the visible output. Impact: Produces corrupted responses in production chat UI for enterprise customers, occasionally exposing small metadata markers to end users and causing downstream parse failures. Observed behavior: When the client reconnects after an intermediate proxy swap or browser refresh, the new SSE session starts emitting partial tokens from the previous fragment interleaved with fresh tokens. Expected behavior: New session should only stream new tokens or a well-defined resume event; no stray metadata or interleaved fragments should be rendered. Workaround: Client-side filter to drop server-sent events containing the legacy resume marker pattern and re-request the full response. This is applied by the customer but is not ideal for UX or cost.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use enterprise account behind corporate proxy that performs transparent TLS interception.
2) Open chat UI connected to SSE endpoint with long-running generation (>30s).
3) While streaming, trigger a network path change: browser refresh, VPN toggle, or proxy re-auth.
4) Observe the new SSE stream: UI shows short duplicated metadata markers and interleaved pieces of previous assistant output.
5) Reproduce with both our JS SDK and a raw EventSource client to rule out SDK parsing bugs.

investigation_notes: Initial triage by Support: replicated behavior with customer sample requests and proxy simulator (staged MITM).
Hypothesis A: proxy is re-ordering or buffering SSE frames and fragments; server ASSISTANT tokens and meta markers merged on re-attach.
Hypothesis B: gateway's connection handoff creates two overlapping worker streams that both emit terminal markers; client stitches them together.

Reproduction: raw EventSource reproduces interleaved 'meta' markers only when an upstream proxy tears TLS mid-stream and resumes with a new TCP flow. No issue when direct-to-backend connection is used.
Server logs show two close/open cycles within 500ms with identical request id headers but different connection ids, suggesting a connection handoff.

2026-03-01 17:05 - SRE (Marco Diaz): Confirmed two backend streams observed. Opening thread with gateway team to check connection multiplexing semantics.
2026-03-02 09:12 - Customer (ClearLedger) via CS: They can reproduce on Chrome/Edge behind company proxy; workaround (client filter) acceptable short-term but impacts UX.

2026-03-02 13:45 - Runtime Eng (Lina Chen): Running focused test injecting synthetic resume markers to observe assembly logic. Suspect resume marker placement logic treats identical request id as in-flight continuation.
resolution: Action plan (in progress): 1) Add server-side dedup guard to ignore resume markers when prior connection did not emit an end-of-stream; 2) Harden gateway to avoid emitting partial fragments during handoff; 3) Provide a small SDK patch to filter known internal meta tokens while we deploy server fix.
Short-term mitigation deployed: SDK v1.4.3 includes opt-in 'sseMetaFilter' that silences internal resume markers. Customer enabled and reports visible token leakage reduced by ~95%.
Follow-ups: Create postmortem runbook for proxy-induced handoffs, coordinate with platform/gateway teams, and add integration test simulating TLS rekey and proxy rehome.
